record.paper_title: Developments and open problems on chiral polytopes
record.original_question: Classify all infinite chiral 4-polytopes in Euclidean 4-space E^4.

evidence.quote: Problem 39 Classify all infinite chiral 4-polytopes in E4.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
An abstract polytope of rank n is a partially ordered set, with a maximum and a minimum element, whose elements (faces) are graded by ranks from -1 to n, in which every maximal chain (flag) has exactly n+2 elements, that satisfies the diamond condition (between any face of rank i-1 and any incident face of rank i+1 there are exactly two faces of rank i) and that is strongly flag-connected. Such a polytope is called chiral if its automorphism group has exactly two orbits on the flags, with adjacent flags lying in distinct orbits (so that the polytope admits maximal rotational symmetry but no reflection symmetry).

A geometric realization of an abstract polytope of rank n in Euclidean d-space E^d is a faithful realization in which the i-faces are realized as suitable geometric figures (vertices, edges, polygons, etc.) and whose combinatorial automorphisms are induced by isometries of E^d. The polytope is said to be infinite if it has infinitely many faces.

Problem: Classify, up to similarity of E^4, all infinite chiral abstract 4-polytopes that admit a faithful geometric realization in Euclidean 4-space E^4 with combinatorial automorphism group induced by isometries of E^4.
artifact.status_search_result: Recent literature on chiral polytopes (e.g. results showing chiral polytopes of full rank exist only in ranks 4 and 5, and constructions of infinite families of chiral 4-polytopes) has made substantial progress, but no source found provides a complete classification of all infinite chiral 4-polytopes geometrically realized in E^4. The problem appears to remain open, with partial results in the full-rank/skeletal setting.

status_evidence.title: Chiral polytopes of full rank exist only in ranks 4 and 5
status_evidence.snippet: Skeletal chiral polytopes of rank n in a Euclidean space must have as ambient space E^d for some d ≥ n if finite, or d ≥ n-1 if infinite... a chiral polytope of full rank can only have rank 4 or 5.
status_evidence.claim: Provides only a partial structural restriction; no full classification of infinite chiral 4-polytopes in E^4.

status_evidence.title: A Finite Chiral 4-Polytope in R^4
status_evidence.snippet: Constructs a finite chiral 4-polytope in R^4.
status_evidence.claim: Classification work on chiral 4-polytopes in E^4 is still being developed via individual examples.

status_evidence.title: Symmetry of Polytopes and Polyhedra (handbook chapter)
status_evidence.snippet: Survey of symmetric polytopes; classification of chiral polytopes in Euclidean spaces is incomplete in higher rank.
status_evidence.claim: Survey indicates classification of infinite chiral 4-polytopes in E^4 is not complete.
